question: The Gaziantep Islamic Science and Technology University (GIBTU) has been receiving EU funding for several years, including from Erasmus+ (KA131-HED) and the European Solidarity Corps. However, serious concerns are surfacing regarding the compatibility of this support with EU values.

Since October 2024, GIBTU has been organising and promoting events glorifying the attacks of 7 October, calling them ‘a turning point in history that upheld the honour of the Ummah’, and circulating anti-Israeli slogans. In October 2025, the university hosted a forum bringing together controversial politico-religious figures, including the President of the Turkish National Agency, İlker Astarci.

He has also appeared in public alongside the GIBTU rector, and renewed the university’s EU funding in August 2025. Despite all this, the Commission tasked the Turkish National Agency with investigating whether GIBTU should be sanctioned. 1.
Why was this assessment handed over to an organisation headed by a president with public and ideological ties to GIBTU?
Does the Commission believe that GIBTU’s recent activities are in keeping with EU values and warrant access to EU funding?
Does it intend to hand the investigation over to an independent body and to suspend funding if the allegations are confirmed?
Supporters1
This question is supported by Members other than the authors: Julie Rechagneux (PfE), Nikola Bartůšek (PfE), Thierry Mariani (PfE), Geadis Geadi (ECR), Fabrice Leggeri (PfE).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.3.2026) The Commission is politically committed and legally bound to ensure that parties receiving EU funding are not involved in criminal or unethical practices, terrorism-related offences, or activities incompatible with EU values.

Pursuant to the Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps Regulations1, the Commission entrusted the implementation of the programmes’ funds through indirect management to the National Agency in Türkiye designated by the competent Turkish national authority. The Director of the Turkish National Agency is an official designated by the Turkish administration and the legal representative of the Agency.

He is overseeing the agency, that is responsible for managing the project lifecycle of the actions, including monitoring beneficiary organisations. Staff members of the agency are Turkish civil servants recruited under national administrative procedure. They sign the declaration of lack of conflict of interest.

Article 19 of the Erasmus+ Regulation requires the Commission to protect the financial interests of the EU. The rules on exclusion of entities from EU funding laid down in Articles 137 to 147 of the Financial Regulation2 apply to Erasmus+ beneficiaries. If the Commission determines that an entity is in an exclusion situation, steps will be taken to protect the EU’s financial interests.

The Commission may flag such entities in the Early Detection and Exclusion System (EDES). It may also instruct the National Agency to suspend or terminate ongoing grant agreements with that entity, and, if appropriate, recover paid grant amounts. The analysis of Gaziantep Islam Science and Technology University activities and investigation are ongoing. The Commission does not intend to involve external bodies for it.
1 Regulation (EU) 2021/817 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 May 2021 establishing

Erasmus+: the Union Programme for education and training, youth and sport and repealing Regulation (EU) No 1288/2013, OJ L 189, 28.5.2021 p.1, Regulation (EU) 2021/888 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 May 2021 establishing the European Solidarity Corps Programme and repealing Regulations (EU) 2018/1475 and (EU) No 375/2014, OJ L 202, 8.6.2021 p.32.

2 Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 September 2024 on the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the Union (recast), OJ L, 2024/2509, 26.9.2024.
